headline: Approved June minutes, appointed two representatives to Urban Media Arts board and subcommittee, and set October 22 for MBTA forum.
summary: Members gave updates on the Lions Club, Disability Pride Month, grants, and Vision 2026 focus areas. They approved the June minutes, named representatives to the Urban Media Arts board and subcommittee, and agreed to hold an MBTA accessibility forum at City Hall on October 22. No one spoke during public comment.
decisions: Approved June 2026 minutes by unanimous roll call vote.
Appointed Lisa Picardi to the Urban Media Arts subcommittee and Shanti Chilukuri to the Urban Media Arts board by unanimous roll call vote.
Agreed to hold the MBTA accessibility forum in a room at City Hall on October 22.
Continued discussion of a possible Commission social gathering to a future meeting.

plain_text:
1 | Page  
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
Disability Commission Meeting Minutes 
September 10, 2026 
 
 
 
Attendance: 
 
 
This meeting took place at 215 Pleasant Street, City Hall, in Room 105 and included remote 
participation. Some members of the Disability Commission participated in the meeting 
remotely per the Governor’s legislation of March 28, 2025, suspending certain provisions of 
the open meeting law. A Microsoft Teams link was also provided for members of the public 
who wished to attend remotely. 
 
This meeting was also recorded through Microsoft Teams and called to order at 6:03PM. 
 
1.  Roll call of Committee Members 
Chuks started the meeting and mentioned that it would be recorded via Microsoft 
Teams. He then called attendance as indicated in the chart above and a quorum was 
present to conduct business. Each member gave a self-description when responding 
to roll call.   
 
2. Approval of Meeting Minutes 
The June 2026 minutes were discussed and upon motion of Kate D. to approve the 
June minutes, seconded by Marilyn, the Commission voted unanimously by roll call 
vote to approve the minutes.  
 
The July 2026 minutes will be taken up at the next meeting since there was not a 
quorum of members who were present at that meeting to vote on their approval. 
 
 
 
 
√ Marilyn Andrews  
√ Shanti Chilukuri 
√ Kate Doyle (in person) 
√ Chukwuka Ezewuzie, Chair  
 Kathleen Higgins 
 Ralph Long  
√ Lisa Picardi  
√ Maria Luise (ADA Compliance Oﬃcer) (in person)  
City 
 
of 
             MASSACHUSETTS 
www.cityofmalden.org 
  Gary Christenson, Mayor
2 | Page  
 
3. Updates or Action Items that need to be Addressed and Current Projects: 
• Lions Club collaboration update: Chuks provided an update on the ongoing 
collaboration with the Lions Club. He reported that discussions with the 
Library Director would resume now that summer had ended. The next step 
was to organize a meeting at the Library to view the physical space. He would 
keep the group informed.  
• Disability Pride Month Event: Lisa provided a recap of the event, which 
included a ﬂag-raising and a proclamation by the Mayor. She noted that she 
and Chuks gave speeches and that there was a great turnout and positive 
atmosphere. Maria thanked Lisa for her help in organizing the event and for 
helping setting up coﬀee and snacks after the ceremony. 
 
• MOD Grant: Maria reported that the Mass Office of Disability has not yet 
issued decisions on grant applications for this cycle. The Commission has  
submitted a request for funds to improve accessibility of the City website.   
• Vision 2026: Commission members provided updates on their respective 
Vision 2026 focus areas: 
• Transportation and Infrastructure: Lisa reported on her ongoing work 
with Malden Safe Streets, including the forum that was organized with 
the three State Senate candidates. Some of the questions focused on 
disability issues.  
• Education Initiatives: Marilyn described participation in forums on new 
restraint laws, disability employment, and workforce support, and 
planned to send a calendar of events for the Malden Special Education 
Parent Advisor Council, including a special education audit presentation. 
Marilyn will also invite Amanda Spartichino to speak at the November 
meeting. Amanda is with the NortheastArc Autism Support Center.  
• Social Activities and Health: Kate D. reported that the All Abilities Bird 
Walk and Resource Fair was a success. The hope is to continue the 
collaboration with DJ Josey and Molina Health.   
• Employment Activities: Maria reported a successful summer youth 
employment program which included coordinating with Kelli Collomb 
and her students at the high school. The program works to 
accommodate students of all abilities. The Commission discussed having 
Kelli attend a future meeting to talk about her program. 
• Housing Advocacy: Chuks explained that he is often approached by 
elderly community members regarding housing and he planned to 
consult with Paul Weston, chair of the Human Rights and Fair Housing 
Commission to see if they are aware of any income-based options for 
elderly and persons with disabilities. Maria also mentioned that at some 
point, we could have someone from the City’s Housing Stability Office 
speak at a meeting as a guest.    
  
  
4.   New Business
3 | Page  
 
• Appointment of Commission Representative to the Urban Media Arts (UMA) 
Board: Chuks asked for volunteers and facilitated the selection of Commission 
representation on UMA's board and subcommittee. After discussion, Lisa 
Picardi was nominated to serve on the subcommittee, and Shanti Chilukuri 
was nominated for the board. Upon motion of Maria, seconded by Marilyn, 
the Commission voted unanimously by roll call vote to appoint Lisa and Shanti 
to the Commission representatives. 
• MBTA Accessibility Presentation: Maria shared that an MBTA representative 
is hoping to present accessibility improvements and upgrades to the MBTA as 
well as other information and resources available. The plan would be for the 
Disability Commission to host a forum and to include outreach to seniors and 
the broader community. The Commission also discussed the pros and cons of 
hosting at the Senior Center and an area of concern was with technology 
requirements for slides and virtual participation. The better option was to use 
a room at City Hall. After reviewing available dates, the Commission agreed 
that October 22nd would be the better date and would allow time for 
publicity and community engagement. Lisa volunteered to assist with the 
event due to its relevance to transportation, and Maria agreed to loop Lisa 
into communications with MBTA. 
• Chuks led a discussion about a possible social gathering of the Commission to 
foster camaraderie, with members discussing potential dates and venues. 
Ultimately, it was decided to revisit details at a future meeting and possibly tie 
the event to the holidays. 
No further business discussed. 
  
5. Public Comment 
No one spoke for public comment.  
 
6.   Scheduling of next meeting and adjournment 
The next meeting was scheduled for Thursday, September 8 at 6:00PM. Upon the 
motion of Maria to adjourn, which was seconded by Kate D. the Commission voted 
unanimously to adjourn the meeting.
